content.text: {"claims":[{"claim":1,"text":"Reactive extrusion of starch–protein blends enables control of mechanical and barrier properties through systematic variation of barrel temperature, screw speed, and protein content.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02373","field":"abstract","quote":"central composite design was used to map the effect of barrel temperature, screw speed, and sunflower protein concentrate content on mechanical and barrier properties"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-02398","field":"abstract","quote":"Pea protein isolate was melt-blended with corn starch at protein contents of 10, 20, and 30 wt%"}]},{"claim":2,"text":"Citric acid promotes cross-linking between starch and protein phases, improving tensile strength from 8.4 MPa to 14.7 MPa and reducing water vapour transmission rate by 29%.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-02398","field":"abstract","quote":"Cross-linking between starch hydroxyl groups and protein amino acid residues was promoted by adding citric acid as a reactive compatibiliser"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-02398","field":"abstract","quote":"Tensile strength of compression-moulded films increased from 8.4 MPa to 14.7 MPa at 20 wt% PPI"},{"id":"SYN-PUB-02398","field":"abstract","quote":"Water vapour transmission rate decreased by 29% relative to unfilled TPS at the same formulation"}]},{"claim":3,"text":"Scale-up of starch–protein extrusion requires adjusted barrel temperature profiles to maintain equivalent gelatinisation degrees when specific mechanical energy decreases at pilot scale.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-10760","field":"abstract","quote":"specific mechanical energy decreased by 23% at pilot scale at equivalent screw speed and temperature, necessitating adjusted barrel temperature profiles to maintain equivalent gelatinisation degrees"}]}]}
